ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, shareholders, and UBOs against: (i) FINTRAC's politically exposed persons (PEP) definition under SOR/2002-184, Part 2; (ii) Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) AML/ATF guidelines; (iii) Canada's sanctions list under the Special Economic Measures Act (S.C. 1992, c. 17), Justice Laws website; (iv) United Nations Security Council Consolidated List (Canada implements UNSC sanctions via SEMA); (v) Canada's Anti-Terrorism Act, 2012, s. 83.05 (listed entities); (vi) OFAC SDN list (for cross-border USD transactions); and (vii) HM Treasury UK sanctions list if the company seeks UK banking relationships. Screening must be continuous, and any MATCH must be escalated to FINTRAC and the BC Registrar of Companies. For a low-risk B2B MRO ecommerce entity, risk rating remains low but standard enhanced due diligence applies to any non-resident UBO with political exposure in a high-risk jurisdiction.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: BC Registry Online (BC Corporate Online) – https://www.corporateonline.gov.bc.ca (managed by the BC Registrar of Companies, Ministry of Finance)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Names must generally be in English, French, or a language with a permissible transliteration; the BC Registry requires a distinctly identifiable name using letters of the Latin alphabet; numeric characters may only appear if the number is part of a word or otherwise permitted by policy; the name must be in the exact form appearing on the incorporation application; any special characters, accents, or punctuation are reviewed on a case-by-case basis; a name proposed in Chinese characters must be transliterated into a romanized equivalent; the registry does not accept names exclusively in non-Latin scripts unless a transliteration is provided and is deemed distinctive under section 24 of the Business Corporations Regulation.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Canada (when used in first position unless authorized)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A name reservation may be extended by paying the prescribed fee of CAD 30 per extension, each extension valid for an additional 56 days, up to a maximum of two extensions. If the registry rejects a proposed name (NRP decision), the applicant may: (1) request a reconsideration within 30 days of the refusal by writing to the Director of Corporate and Public Registry, Ministry of Finance, BC, providing a written submission and a copy of the rejection notice; (2) file a new name reservation request with a wholly different name; or (3) if reconsideration fails, seek judicial review in the Supreme Court of British Columbia under the Judicial Review Procedure Act, R.S.B.C. 1996, c. 241, within 60 days of the reconsideration decision. An administrative appeal must attach a copy of the original NRP decision and a statement of the legal and factual basis for why the name should be accepted. The Director has 30–60 days to issue a decision. For urgent incorporations, counsel may simultaneously incorporate under a numerical designation (e.g., 1234567 B.C. Ltd.) and apply for a change of name thereafter.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible but subject to strict conditions. Under s. 53 of the Business Corporations Act (BC), the registered office must be a physical address in British Columbia at which the corporation’s records and minute books are maintained and at which process may be served during normal business hours. A virtual office provider that provides a physical street address, a dedicated mailing address, and accepts service of process during statutory business hours is acceptable. However, use of a post-office box or a non-physical virtual address is not permissible. The BC Registry requires the registered office to be at a location that is not merely a mail-forwarding address. For an e-commerce MRO supplies business that does not maintain an inventory warehouse in BC, a virtual office is accepted as long as the provider is a licensed corporate services provider or law firm that can receive legal process and forward maintains records. Physical on-site inspection likelihood: Low-to-Moderate for the corporate registry; the BC Registrar does not conduct routine unannounced inspections of registered offices for ordinary business corporations. However, if the company is selected for a compliance review, a spot-check visit to the registered office may occur to verify that it is not a mail-only address. For an e-commerce company with no inventory on site, the likelihood of an unannounced inspection is below 5% annually (based on registry administrative risk). FINTRAC may conduct unannounced on-site examinations of the corporate’s compliance program if the company is a reporting entity under the PCMLTFA. Since this entity is e-commerce and not selling money services, FINTRAC AML compliance obligations are limited to reporting suspicious transactions and certain recordkeeping; OSFI does not typically inspect non-FI entities. The quantified risk of physical inspection for the registered office is 2%–5% in the first three years, increase to 15% if the VC address is a high-density shared office center flagged for shell companies.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act, SBC 2002, c. 57 (British Columbia): s. 10 (application for incorporation), s. 11 (notice of articles), s. 12 (certificate of incorporation), s. 14 (articles), s. 49-50 (share capital), s. 191 (registered office), s. 195 (records), s. 197-198 (directors), s. 254 (corporate seals). Provincial incorporation selected per jurisdiction CA_BC; federal Canada Business Corporations Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-44, not elected.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: BC Corporate Registry, Ministry of Finance, Province of British Columbia (Corporate Online portal)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Incorporation (Form 2) together with Notice of Articles (Form 3) and Articles (Form 1)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital and no escrow account requirement. Shares may be issued at any consideration (including nominal or par value of CAD 0.01), and the company may incorporate with one or more incorporators; the company commences existence upon issuance of the Certificate of Incorporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the Certificate of Incorporation, Articles, and Notice of Articles filed under the Business Corporations Act (British Columbia) are ratified in their entirety. RESOLVED that the Company issue one hundred common shares to the named subscriber at CAD 1.00 per share, subscription proceeds being fully received and credited to stated capital. RESOLVED that the registered office be established at [Registered Office Address], British Columbia, with [Corporate Records Agent] appointed as records agent. RESOLVED that [Director] is appointed President and Chief Executive Officer, [Director] Secretary, and [Director] Treasurer, each to serve until successors are appointed. RESOLVED that management is authorized to open bank accounts, execute contracts, and complete all statutory filings required to commence operations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Corporate Online / OneStop Business Registry, Province of British Columbia
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a NUANS corporate name search through a BC-registered search house or BC Corporate Online. If a distinctive name is desired, file a Name Reservation Request (CAD 30) reserving the name for 56 days. Alternatively, proceed with a numbered name (e.g., 1234567 B.C. Ltd.) and register a trade name after incorporation.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate name (up to three alternatives)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected for confusing similarity, submit revised name choices or file a reconsideration request with the Registrar supported by a written submission distinguishing the marks.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting of Articles and Notice of Articles
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Qualified legal counsel; incorporators' pre-filing review
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Articles (Form 1) prescribing the authorized share structure (common shares without par value), director count, and any permitted share transfer restrictions; complete Notice of Articles (Form 3) stating the registered office, directors, and share structure; execute the Incorporation Application (Form 2) and consents to act as director, ensuring compliance with ss. 10-11 of the Business Corporations Act, SBC 2002, c. 57, with the statutory Model Articles incorporated by reference to fill any gaps.
required_dossiers: Form 5 — Consent to Act as Director (or equivalent clause in Articles)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry identifies incomplete or defective provisions, amend and refile the affected forms prior to issuance; gap-filling default provisions in the Act apply automatically unless excluded.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory Filing and Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Corporate Registry, Ministry of Finance (Corporate Online portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the incorporation application electronically through Corporate Online, pay the CAD 350 filing fee, and receive expedited processing. Upon approval, the Registrar of Companies issues the Certificate of Incorporation, at which point the company has legal personality under s. 12 of the Act; download and retain the certificate, incorporation number, and certified Notice of Articles.
required_dossiers: Approved name reservation (if a distinctive name is used)
Duly executed Form 1, Form 2, and Form 3
Credit card or Corporate Online account payment confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is placed under examination or rejected, correct the deficiency within the Registry's 90-day resubmission window; switching to a numbered company avoids name-related delay and preserves priority.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Federal Business Number and Tax Account Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) — Business Registration Online (BRO)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register with the CRA to obtain the 9-digit Business Number (BN) and program accounts: GST/HST (mandatory once taxable supplies exceed CAD 30,000 in any quarter or cumulatively over four consecutive quarters, but advisable voluntarily at incorporation to claim input tax credits), payroll deductions account if employees are hired, corporate income tax account, and an import/export account if goods cross borders. Use the incorporation number and describe the activity as NAICS 423840.
required_dossiers: Directors' full names, personal addresses, and dates of birth
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the BN application triggers identity verification, respond to CRA correspondence within 30 days with certified corporate documents; late GST/HST registration penalties may be reduced or waived under the voluntary disclosure program.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Provincial Registrations and Municipal Business Licence
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: OneStop Business Registry; WorkSafeBC; BC Ministry of Finance (PST Division); local municipal licensing office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Use OneStop to register for the BC Provincial Sales Tax (PST) vendor account, WorkSafeBC firm coverage, and the municipal business licence applicable to the warehouse and registered office address. Complete the municipal zoning and occupancy review for the physical warehouse; for electronic catalog B2B MRO retail, no sectoral statutory operating licence is mandated, but the municipal licence, building occupancy permit, and property tax enrollment must be secured before physical operations commence.
required_dossiers: Lease agreement or title evidence for the premises
Site plan and zoning certificate from the municipality
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipality refuses a business licence on zoning grounds, apply for a variance or temporary use permit; adverse decisions may be appealed to the Board of Variance and subsequently by judicial review to the Supreme Court of British Columbia.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: BC Ministry of Environment and Climate Change Strategy (MOECCS); municipal planning and fire departments; WorkSafeBC
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Municipal Business Licence (general operations); no sectoral statutory operating permit is required under federal or provincial law for electronic catalog retail and distribution of industrial maintenance, repair, and operations hardware

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — not a 'reviewable project' under the Environmental Assessment Act, SBC 2002, c. 43, Schedule 2; indoor warehousing and catalog distribution activities do not trigger any project designation threshold
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Sanitary wastewater must comply with the applicable municipal sewer and drainage bylaw; airborne VOC emissions are negligible from packaging operations and remain below applicable CCME ambient air quality objectives; packaging waste is subject to the BC Recycling Regulation; any spent batteries, oils, or chemical MRO goods are handled under the Hazardous Waste Regulation; transport of dangerous goods (including aerosol or solvent-based products) must comply with the Transportation of Dangerous Goods Act, 1992 and WHMIS labeling requirements.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Occupancy permit and annual fire safety inspection under the BC Fire Code; structural load approval for pallet racking and mezzanine installations through a professional engineer; WorkSafeBC compliance clearance for warehousing operations under the OHS Regulation (Part 4 general conditions, Part 14 material handling, Part 15 rigging); municipal building permit for tenant improvements; a formal occupational health and safety program and first aid assessment are required once workers are engaged.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) - federal tax administration portal 'My Business Account' (https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/e-services/digital-services-businesses/business-account.html); BC provincial indirect tax administered by the BC Ministry of Finance via eTaxBC (https://etax.gov.bc.ca).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1) Incorporate under the Canada Business Corporations Act (CBCA) or BC Business Corporations Act (SBC 2002, c. 57) via Corporations Canada Online Filing Centre or BC Corporate Online; 2) CRA automatically issues a 9-digit Business Number (BN) to the newly incorporated federal/provincial company; 3) Open federal program accounts through CRA Business Registration Online (BRO) - RT (GST/HST), RC (corporate income tax), RP (payroll), RM (import/export); 4) Register for BC PST via eTaxBC (Form PV100 / online account; vendor registration mandatory when taxable sales in BC exceed CAD 10,000 per calendar year); 5) Non-resident vendors selling physical MRO goods into Canada use CRA Form RC1 to obtain the BN and may be required to register under Section 240(1.1) of the Excise Tax Act when carrying on business in Canada through an agent or permanent establishment.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation - a resident Canadian corporation is taxed under ITA Part I on worldwide income at the combined federal 15% + BC 12% general corporate rate (27%); no check-the-box or pass-through eligibility; a non-resident-owned corporation is still a Canadian resident if incorporated in Canada (ITA s. 250(4)(a)); foreign shareholders are subject to Part XIII withholding on dividends (25% under the ITA, potentially reduced to 5%/15% under an applicable tax treaty).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box election exists under Canadian law; US LLC/partnership entities are per se taxable corporations. Available elections include: ITA s. 261 functional-currency election, CCA class elections under Income Tax Regulations s. 1100, ETA s. 156 election for closely related corporations to exclude internal taxable supplies from GST/HST, and foreign-affiliate clean-surplus/capital-dividend elections (ITA ss. 93(1) and 83(2)). Hybrid-mismatch ordering rules (ITA ss. 18.4, 18.6, 18.6.1) apply from July 1, 2022 and disallow deductions for payments that are deductible in Canada but not included in the recipient's jurisdiction without any elective override; use of an unlimited liability company (ULC) may trigger entity-classification mismatches in cross-border planning.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (federal value-added tax at 5%) plus BC Provincial Sales Tax (PST at 7%); combined headline rate in British Columbia is 12%.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 (GST/HST small-supplier threshold); the threshold is tested on the total consideration from taxable supplies made in Canada in the last four consecutive calendar quarters and, for corporations, also in any single calendar quarter. BC PST: registration is required once a vendor's taxable sales of tangible personal property in BC exceed CAD 10,000 per calendar year (small-vendor exemption).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada does not mandate real-time fiscal clearance, API pre-clearance, or digital stamping for e-invoices. Electronic filing of GST/HST returns is compulsory for registrants whose annual worldwide taxable revenues exceed CAD 1.5 million (GST/HST NETFILE or EDI); BC PST returns are paperless through eTaxBC. B2B e-invoicing is voluntary and may adopt PEPPOL/EBMS; CRA record-retention rules require 6 years of supporting books and records in Canada.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under Part V of Schedule VI to the Excise Tax Act: (1) zero-rated if the supplier ships the tangible personal property (MRO hardware) to a destination outside Canada and possession passes at that destination; (2) if a GST/HST-registered recipient removes the goods from Canada, zero-rating applies where the recipient exports the goods within 60 days of delivery and retains proof of export; (3) services performed on goods that are exported (drop-ship/logistics support, technical documentation) may be zero-rated under s. 7 of Part V when supplied to a non-resident or in respect of exported tangible property; (4) sales delivered within BC attract 5% GST + 7% PST unless the purchaser obtains a direct-pay/exemption certificate; advertising/promotional expenses for the catalog are subject to GST/HST under the place-of-supply rules.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: CBSA Canada Customs Export Declaration (B13A) filed via the Canadian International Trade Single Window (CITSW)/G7 customs reporting
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill evidencing physical shipment to the foreign consignee and foreign destination
Inward remittance records (bank credit advice/SWIFT MT103) evidencing receipt of export consideration from the foreign buyer
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA's normal reassessment window is 4 years, extended indefinitely where a taxpayer has made misrepresentation or fraud; unwarranted zero-rating claims are clawed back with daily compounded prescribed-rate interest. Civil gross-negligence penalty under ETA s. 285.1 is 25% of the tax sought to be evaded; criminal prosecution under ETA s. 329 carries, on indictment, fines up to 50% of the evaded tax and/or 5 years imprisonment. Every export claim must be substantiated contemporaneously by B13A export declarations, shipping/waybills, and remittance evidence; failure results in retrospective GST/PST assessments, denial of input tax credits/refunds, penalties, and denial of the 0% rate for both GST and BC PST.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada); cross-border funds-transfer administration is shared with FINTRAC and the Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA), but Canada has no dedicated exchange-control authority.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar (CAD) is fully convertible under IMF Article VIII. Capital-account and current-account transactions are generally free from exchange-control approval, including capital injections, intercompany loans, trade settlements, and profit repatriation. Dividend remittances are subject to Part XIII non-resident withholding tax, normally 25% statutory or reduced under an applicable income tax treaty. Practical remittance hurdles include source-of-funds verification, FATCA/CRS beneficial-ownership reporting, Investment Canada Act notification in the narrow case of an acquisition of control, and the bank's own sanctions and anti-money-laundering screening.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Not applicable. Canada imposes no export-proceeds surrender requirement, no mandatory repatriation timeline, and no prescribed conversion ratio. Exporters may retain export receivables indefinitely in CAD or any freely convertible foreign currency. Statutory timeline: none. Mandatory conversion ratio: 0%. Cross-border currency movements of CAD 10,000 or more require a CBSA/FINTRAC declaration for reporting purposes only and do not create surrender or conversion obligations.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Royal Bank of Canada (RBC Royal Bank)
The Toronto-Dominion Bank (TD Canada Trust / TD Commercial Banking)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Conditional Medium. Off-shore digital EMIs such as Wise, Airwallex, and Currenxie are feasible as secondary cross-border payment vehicles for B2B MRO catalogue receipts and supplier disbursements, but they are not chartered banks and cannot replace a domestic Schedule I bank operating account. Funds held with EMIs are typically in omnibus or partner-bank accounts, which creates counterparty and ring-fencing risk. If the offshore EMI solicits customers in Canada or provides Canadian-facing remittance services, it may require FINTRAC Money Service Business registration and provincial money-services licences. For prudential safety, large-value CAD and USD treasury flows must settle through Payments Canada and SWIFT correspondent accounts at a Canadian chartered bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote opening is permitted under Canadian AML/KYC rules, and there is no statutory requirement for directors to appear physically for a British Columbia business corporation. Most Tier 1 banks require a video interview with at least one director or senior officer, notarized corporate resolutions, and pre-verified identity documents. For foreign parent structures with no local business substance, banks may impose in-person branch interview conditions, physical lease inspection, and certified passport copies before activating the account.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Multi-layer foreign beneficial ownership with entities in the US, APAC, and EU supply chain
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: BC Business Registry extract, federal corporations Canada profile, Certificate of Incumbency, register of directors and shareholders, beneficial-ownership attestation, source-of-wealth statements for each material UBO, audited or reviewed financial statements, notarized consent to share bank records, and a funds-flow ownership chart.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between declared B2B e-commerce catalogue revenue and high-frequency, low-value cross-border credit-card and SWIFT wire flows
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed customer and supplier contracts, sample invoices with purchase orders, payment-gateway merchant statements, logistics and customs export records, website catalogue captures, ISIC/NAICS business-activity evidence, and rolling revenue forecasts.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large inbound intercompany capital contribution shortly after incorporation
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board and shareholder resolutions approving the capital subscription or loan, contributed-surplus declaration, executed intercompany loan agreement, remittance purpose-code narrative, source-of-funds bank statements, CRA filing history, and a documented treasury funds-flow diagram.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payments to higher-risk jurisdictions or conflict-sensitive suppliers of industrial MRO hardware
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Counterparty sanctions-screening results, export classification and end-use certificates, Incoterms schedules, detailed HTS/HS commodity descriptions, manufacturer letters of authorization, supplier KYC packs, and the entity's FINTRAC-compliant AML procedure manual.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident director profile and registered-agent only substance in BC
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: BC premises lease or sublease, Canadian payroll or contractor records, utility and local phone bills, corporate operating plan, website and platform seller-verification evidence, and retained video interview recordings stored for AML audit purposes.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Structure as SWIFT MT103 with remittance purpose code 'INTC' or narrative 'CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION' referencing the subscribed amount. The Canadian receiving bank will require a source-of-funds questionnaire, board resolution authorizing the injection, BC corporate registry proof, and a funds-flow statement. No Bank of Canada exchange-control filing is required. If the capital injection is part of a greenfield corporate set-up, the transaction is not an Investment Canada Act reviewable acquisition of control. CAD funds settle through Payments Canada Lynx; USD funds settle through a US correspondent bank over Fedwire or CHIPS.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use SWIFT MT103 for open-account supplier settlements, documentary letters of credit (MT700/MT710, commonly irrevocable at sight) for high-value MRO procurements, and SWIFT MT202 for bank-to-bank cover where required. The CAD leg clears domestically via Payments Canada Lynx or Real-Time Rail; the USD leg clears via the Canadian bank's US correspondent through Fedwire or CHIPS. Supporting trade documentation must include invoices, packing lists, bills of lading, inspection certificates, and Incoterms-based delivery verification. Commercial credit-card settlement remains acceptable only for low-value catalogue transactions and must not replace wire or LC rails for large trade disbursements.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Vanilla deliverable FX forwards (CAD/USD and other freely convertible pairs)
Rolling FX forwards with flexible fixing dates
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for currencies that are not freely deliverable in Canada
Vanilla FX options, including purchased calls, purchased puts, and simple zero-premium combinations
CME-listed FX futures and options on futures for exchange-traded counterparty mitigation

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: British Columbia Annual Report under the Business Corporations Act
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: BC Registry, Ministry of Citizens' Services
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within two months after the annual anniversary date of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty CAD 100; continued failure triggers administrative strike-off proceedings under BCBCA s. 271, resulting in loss of corporate capacity and potential dissolution.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No shareholder threshold applies. BCBCA requires appointment of an independent auditor at each annual general meeting unless all shareholders unanimously consent to waive the audit for that year. Public companies and entities with regulatory securities filings are subject to audit without waiver.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS for public companies; ASPE (CPA Canada Handbook Part II) is permissible for private enterprises

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No separate annual beneficial-ownership confirmation is filed with BC Registry. Share transfers are recorded in the register of members, and director names are updated on the annual report. A shareholder list or register inspection is only available upon meeting common-law and statutory requirements.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,500–8,000 for a low-risk B2B MRO e-commerce private company when an audit is not waived
